read.thesis: Jabil raised FY26 revenue to $32.4B (+$1.1B), core margin to ~5.7% and core EPS to $11.55, with AI revenue now $12.1B (+35%) and capacity utilisation rising from ~75% toward ~80%.

utilisation.quote: Our capacity utilization has gone up from that 75% range, closer to the 80% range.

capex.quote: The CapEx outlook has been 1.5% to 2% of revenue, and that's going to remain consistent for FY '26.

triggers.label: Utilisation 75% → ~80%
triggers.quote: Our capacity utilization has gone up from that 75% range, closer to the 80% range.

triggers.label: FY26 revenue +$1.1B to $32.4B
triggers.quote: For fiscal 2026, we now expect revenue of approximately $32.4 billion, an increase of $1.1 billion from our prior outlook.

triggers.label: AI revenue 25% → 35% growth
triggers.quote: Altogether, we now expect AI-related revenue of approximately $12.1 billion in fiscal 2026, which represents approximately 35% year-over-year growth, up from 25% originally expected in September.

triggers.label: Gross margin held at 9-9.5% range
triggers.quote: we've always sort of mentioned 9% to 9.5% is the range for our gross margin. That's still the FY '26 estimate.

guidance.quote: For fiscal 2026, we now expect revenue of approximately $32.4 billion, an increase of $1.1 billion from our prior outlook.
We now anticipate core operating margins of roughly 5.7%, a meaningful improvement of 10 basis points versus our earlier view.
we now expect core diluted earnings per share of $11.55 for the year, an increase of $0.55 from our previous estimate.
we expect adjusted free cash flow of more than $1.3 billion, consistent with the framework we outlined in September
total company revenue for Q2 is expected to be in the range of $7.5 billion to $8 billion.
Core diluted earnings per share is expected to be in the range of $2.27 to $2.67.
we've always sort of mentioned 9% to 9.5% is the range for our gross margin. That's still the FY '26 estimate.
The CapEx outlook has been 1.5% to 2% of revenue, and that's going to remain consistent for FY '26.
I think if you're looking at the revenue piece for the second hyperscaler roughly in that $1 billion range.
